title: Two Coworkers Talk About Finding Peace in Little Things
script: Dewi: [thoughtful] Fajar, this week has been so heavy. Meetings, deadlines, more meetings.
Fajar: I know the feeling. How are you managing it?
Dewi: [reflective] Honestly, not very well. I feel tired all the time now.
Fajar: Can I share something that helps me? It sounds small, but it works.
Dewi: [honestly] Please, I need something right now.
Fajar: Every morning, before I open my laptop, I look outside for one minute and say alhamdulillah.
Dewi: [determined] Just one minute? That seems too simple to help.
Fajar: I thought so too, at first. But it reminds me that today is a gift, even a hard day.
Dewi: [warmly] I usually open my phone first thing, and I feel stressed before I even start my coffee.
Fajar: Try it tomorrow. One minute, no phone, just noticing something small you are grateful for.
Dewi: [peacefully] Okay, I will try it. What do you usually notice?
Fajar: Sometimes the sky, sometimes the smell of coffee, sometimes just being alive and healthy.
Dewi: [gently] Does it really change your whole day, just one minute?
Fajar: Not every day, but on most days, yes. It resets something in my head before the stress starts.
Dewi: I think I have forgotten how to notice small things. Everything feels urgent lately.
Fajar: [encouraging] That happens to all of us sometimes. The urgency is not always real, even when it feels real.
Dewi: That's a nice way to start the day. I think I needed to hear this.
Fajar: We all need reminders sometimes. That's what friends are for.
Dewi: [warmly] Okay, tomorrow morning, one minute, no phone. I will tell you how it goes.
Fajar: I'll ask you at lunch. Deal?
